purpose: Private reference question review: evidence-backed source/design claims and scoring reproductions; no generator or learner-outcome certification.

scope.review: All 40 extracted units read; words/dose/open rubrics/fallback marker and selected film/reading delivery code deeply inspected. Includes rubric subchecks, not forty independent measurements.
scope.privacy: No personal metadata names retained; fictional characters retained.

verdict.short: A strong reference for lesson-connected guided practice, with a definite content/key ambiguity and reproducible fallback-scoring defects. Overall high-quality or mastery certification is not established.
what_is_good: Evidence followed by explanation and rebuttal
verdict.claim_strength: Source-supported observations and deterministic reproductions, no calibrated global score.

external_run_observation.interpretation: 14 off-text judge flags are not fourteen adjudicated faults; grammar/meaning contrasts can be valid absent the passage. Three recorded draws support within-run consistency, not accuracy/qualification/tuning isolation/learning gains.

findings.title: Angry has a defensible second destination
findings.claim: General word-to-person prompt makes angry→IAGO IS defensible: the same lesson teaches Iago is angry with Othello. The key accepts only Roderigo. Wrong feedback narrows to who shouts at the beginning only after the attempt.
findings.limits: The authored angry meaning explicitly narrows to furious Roderigo shouting when the scene opens. That explains the intended key but is not a pre-attempt question condition in this renderer: PinWords passes only w.w strings to WordBoard; WordBoard draws word strings only, and the accessible selection buttons also display w.w. Neither component reads meaning. This is a source-code visibility check, not a hosted browser check. The intended distinction is teachable if supplied before the first attempt or scored nonexclusively. One word, not every classification.

findings.title: Fallback drops quotation-to-claim relationship
findings.claim: Character-file requires a quote proving the description; its fallback matches describing-word keywords only. It accepts deceitful plus unrelated Call up her father or invented Purple elephants dance and returns met/File.
findings.limits: Normal UI limits quotations to paragraph/store choices. Invented-quote probes are not established normal learner UI attacks. This is a marker-contract gap partly masked by curated inputs.

findings.title: Smiling asserted as a scene detail
findings.claim: Key-term correct feedback says He smiles at Othello while he plots against him. Preceding source teaches irony/appearance but no explicit smile-at-Othello moment. It illustrates a false front but is not cited textual evidence.
findings.limits: All media frames/stagings were not inspected. Not a claim Iago never smiles in the whole play. The supplied excerpt itself states Othello is not in this scene.

findings.title: Progress after reveal is not successful reasoning
findings.claim: Dose advances after revealing an explanation on the third unsuccessful try; after three unsuccessful rebuttals it reveals and finishes. Progress does not necessarily mean the learner convinced the character.
findings.limits: Can be a legitimate coaching policy. Completion must not be promoted to independent mastery.

recommended_next_validation.first: Replay definite failures, propose source corrections to its owner; preserve original reference.
recommended_next_validation.academic_packet: Original prompt and actual learner context; hide review/model labels; independently resolve ambiguity and feedback.
recommended_next_validation.negative_controls: Reversed relations, negations, irrelevant real quotes, fabricated quotes, legitimate paraphrases; distinguish UI-permitted inputs from API-only probes.
recommended_next_validation.measurement: Separate content validity, runtime marker validity, availability, repeatability and student outcomes.
recommended_next_validation.source_grounding: Use quoted learner-visible text or explicitly label invented illustrations.
